verdict.summary: Wix apps are self-serve: configure permissions in the app dashboard, release a version, and share an install link, with no review for unlisted apps. App Market listing is reviewed by an automated AI check that Wix says typically returns results within minutes. The model differs from classic user OAuth: a site owner installs your app on one site, and your backend mints 4-hour tokens with client_credentials plus that site's instanceId, so the agent acts per site, not per user.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create an app, pick permissions, install it on your own site, capture instanceId from the App Instance Installed webhook or the install redirect, then call POST /oauth2/token.

timeToProd.assumes: An unlisted app distributed with a share install link or the external install flow that reads site data (stores, CRM, bookings); App Market listing goes through an automated review that usually adds minutes, plus fix-and-resubmit loops.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing — no review for unlisted apps. Automated AI review only if you list on the App Market.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Wix says unlisted apps skip review, and App Market AI review results are typically available within minutes. Wix may audit apps retroactively.

prerequisites.item: A Wix account with access to the app dashboard (Custom Apps)
prerequisites.why: Apps, permissions, the OAuth app ID and secret, and install links are all managed there.
You have to release a version before you can distribute an app or create an install link.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS backend that stores instanceId per site
prerequisites.why: Tokens are minted with app ID, app secret and instanceId. The external-install callback has to use HTTPS, and App Market apps have to be served over HTTPS.

prerequisites.item: Privacy policy, Terms of Use and a demo account (App Market only)
prerequisites.why: The guidelines ask for a privacy policy and Terms of Use, and an active demo account with login details for review.

scopeTiers.impact: Permissions are chosen in the app dashboard and granted by the site owner at install. Each API reference lists which permission scopes it accepts. Exact labels vary by API.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The example labels are illustrative. Wix permission names are shown in the dashboard and API reference, which we didn't enumerate.

scopeTiers.impact: Lets an agent change products, orders or content. For App Market listing, request only what's needed and don't stack redundant scopes, for example Manage Products alongside Manage Stores - All Permissions.

examples: App permissions ∩ Wix user role permissions
scopeTiers.impact: Tokens on behalf of a Wix user carry the intersection of app and user permissions, and only work from dashboard page extensions, not an external agent backend.

steps.title: Create an app in the Wix app dashboard
steps.detail: Sign in and create a new self-managed app from Custom Apps. Copy the App ID and App secret from the OAuth page.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: manage.wix.com/account/custom-apps redirected to the Wix sign-in page on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Choose least-privilege permissions
steps.detail: Map each API the agent calls to its permission scopes (listed per endpoint in the REST/SDK reference) and pick the smallest set with no redundant scopes.

steps.title: Configure permissions and webhooks in the dashboard
steps.detail: Add the permissions and subscribe to the App Instance Installed webhook (and any data webhooks). Subscribing can auto-add required permissions.

steps.title: Implement token minting and instanceId storage
steps.detail: On install, verify signedInstance (or the webhook) and store instanceId. Mint tokens with POST https://www.wixapis.com/oauth2/token {grant_type: client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, instance_id}, cache them for under 4 hours, and send them in the Authorization header. Or use @wix/sdk AppStrategy.

steps.title: Release a version
steps.detail: Release a major version of the app in the dashboard. Distribution and install links need one.

steps.title: Install on a test site and verify API calls
steps.detail: Install the app on a site you manage (direct install or install link), grant permissions, and confirm your backend receives instanceId and can call APIs.

steps.title: Build the external install flow for your agent product
steps.detail: Build https://www.wix.com/app-installer?appId=...&shareUrlId=...&postInstallationUrl=<encoded HTTPS callback> with custom state, and handle the redirect (appId, tenantId, instanceId, signedInstance).

steps.title: Share the install link (unlisted go-live)
steps.detail: From Distribute App, choose Share Install Link and put it, or the external install URL, in your product. Any Wix site owner can install it. No review.

steps.title: Optional: prepare and submit an App Market listing
steps.detail: Draft the listing, privacy policy and terms. Prepare a demo account and review notes. Check against the guidelines (Wix Billing for any charges, 400ms startup, no off-platform purchase links, no user-of-user data harvesting).

steps.title: Optional: automated AI review
steps.detail: Submit and publish. The automated review returns pass or blockers, typically within minutes. Fix the blockers and resubmit, or appeal through support.

agentCanDo: Map APIs to minimal Wix permission scopes
Implement instanceId capture, signedInstance verification and token minting
Build the external install URL and callback handler
Draft App Market listing, privacy policy and review notes

Configure permissions and webhooks in the dashboard

blockers.cause: Missing or wrong client_id, client_secret or instance_id. The app may not be installed on that site.
blockers.fix: Send all four fields as JSON and use an instanceId captured from a verified install for this app.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Seen with dummy credentials on 2026-10-20. Wix may return more specific errors for real but mismatched credentials.

blockers.symptom: Can't find a refresh-token endpoint, or legacy code calling 'Refresh an Access Token' fails for a new app
blockers.cause: Custom authentication (code + refresh token) is deprecated for new apps. New apps mint tokens with client_credentials and instanceId.
blockers.fix: Replace refresh calls with Create Access Token and keep instanceId as the long-lived credential.

blockers.symptom: No install link option, or prompted to release a version
blockers.cause: The app has no released major version yet.
blockers.fix: Release a version, then create the share install link.

blockers.symptom: External install from your site doesn't redirect back for an unlisted app
blockers.cause: Unlisted apps need shareUrlId in the installer URL, and postInstallationUrl has to be URI-encoded and HTTPS.
blockers.fix: Add shareUrlId from your share link and encode the callback URL.

blockers.symptom: API call denied despite a valid token
blockers.cause: The app lacks one of the permission scopes listed for that endpoint, or, for user-delegated tokens, the Wix user's role lacks it.
blockers.fix: Add the scope in the dashboard (existing sites may need to approve the change) or use an app-instance token.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: How existing installs re-consent to added permissions wasn't confirmed.

blockers.cause: The automated AI review found guideline violations (permissions, billing, performance, content).
blockers.fix: Resolve each blocker in the dashboard and resubmit, or appeal through Wix support.

nuances.text: Access tokens from POST /oauth2/token are valid for 4 hours, with no refresh token. Mint a new one with client_credentials and instanceId, which acts as the permanent per-site credential.
Verify signedInstance before trusting or storing an instanceId from a redirect, because query parameters can be forged.
Installs are per site, not per user. A customer with several Wix sites installs your app on each one, and each gets its own instanceId.
Wix API keys exist but can't be used by third-party Wix apps, so OAuth via app install is the only third-party path.
The App Market guidelines forbid using CRM, Orders or other user-of-user data to build your own contact database or to sell or share with third parties. Keep agent memory scoped to serving that site.

Any app that collects money has to use the Wix Billing System unless Wix grants an exception, and only the initial listing (or a resubmission after a decline) needs review. Later versions are released without approval but may be audited retroactively.
